title_en: Provisions on Directing the Orientation of Foreign Investment

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Provisions are formulated in accordance with the state's relevant legal provisions on foreign investment and the requirements of industrial policies, for the purposes of guiding the direction of foreign investment, aligning the direction of foreign investment with the national economic and social development plan of China, and facilitating the protection of the legitimate rights and interests of investors.

Article 2 These Provisions shall apply to projects invested in Chinese-foreign equity joint ventures, Chinese-foreign contractual joint ventures, and wholly foreign-owned enterprises (hereinafter referred to as foreign-invested enterprises) within the territory of China, as well as other forms of foreign-invested projects (hereinafter referred to as foreign-invested projects).

Article 3 The Catalogue for the Guidance of Foreign Investment Industries and the Catalogue of Advantaged Industries for Foreign Investment in the Central and Western Regions shall be formulated by the State Development Planning Commission, the State Economic and Trade Commission, and the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation jointly with the relevant departments of the State Council, and shall be promulgated after approval by the State Council; where partial adjustments need to be made to the Catalogue for the Guidance of Foreign Investment Industries and the Catalogue of Advantaged Industries for Foreign Investment in the Central and Western Regions based on actual circumstances, the State Economic and Trade Commission, the State Development Planning Commission, and the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation shall, jointly with the relevant departments of the State Council, make timely revisions and promulgate them.
The Catalogue for the Guidance of Foreign Investment Industries and the Catalogue of Advantaged Industries for Foreign Investment in the Central and Western Regions shall be the basis for guiding the examination and approval of foreign-invested projects and the application of relevant policies by foreign-invested enterprises.

Article 4 Foreign-invested projects shall be classified into four categories: encouraged, permitted, restricted, and prohibited.
Encouraged, restricted, and prohibited foreign-invested projects shall be listed in the Catalogue for the Guidance of Foreign Investment Industries. Foreign-invested projects that do not fall within the categories of encouraged, restricted, or prohibited shall be permitted foreign-invested projects. Permitted foreign-invested projects shall not be listed in the Catalogue for the Guidance of Foreign Investment Industries.

Article 8 The Catalogue for the Guidance of Foreign Investment Industries may stipulate that foreign-invested projects be "limited to joint venture or contractual joint venture," "Chinese-controlled," or "Chinese relatively controlled."
"Limited to joint venture or contractual joint venture" means that only Chinese-foreign equity joint ventures or Chinese-foreign contractual joint ventures are permitted; "Chinese-controlled" means that the aggregate investment proportion of Chinese investors in the foreign-invested project is 51% or more; "Chinese relatively controlled" means that the aggregate investment proportion of Chinese investors in the foreign-invested project is greater than the investment proportion of any single foreign investor.

Article 9 For encouraged foreign-invested projects, in addition to enjoying preferential treatment in accordance with relevant laws and administrative regulations, those engaging in the construction and operation of energy, transportation, and urban infrastructure projects (including coal, petroleum, natural gas, electricity, railways, highways, ports, airports, urban roads, sewage treatment, garbage treatment, etc.) involving large investments and long payback periods may, upon approval, expand their business scope related thereto.

Article 10 Permitted foreign-invested projects whose products are entirely directly exported shall be regarded as encouraged foreign-invested projects; restricted foreign-invested projects whose export sales revenue accounts for 70% or more of their total product sales revenue may, upon approval by the people's government of the province, autonomous region, municipality directly under the Central Government, or city specifically designated in the state plan, or by the competent department of the State Council, be regarded as permitted foreign-invested projects.

Article 11 For permitted and restricted foreign-invested projects that can truly leverage the advantages of the central and western regions, the conditions may be appropriately relaxed; among them, those listed in the Catalogue of Advantaged Industries for Foreign Investment in the Central and Western Regions may enjoy the preferential policies applicable to encouraged foreign-invested projects.

Article 12 In accordance with the current approval authority, foreign-invested projects shall be examined, approved, and filed respectively by the development planning department and the economic and trade department based on the nature of the project; the contracts and articles of association of foreign-invested enterprises shall be examined, approved, and filed by the foreign economic and trade department. Among them, restricted foreign-invested projects below the quota shall be examined and approved by the corresponding competent department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, municipality directly under the Central Government, or city specifically designated in the state plan, and shall be filed with the superior competent department and the industry competent department at the same time; the approval authority for such projects shall not be delegated. Foreign-invested projects in the service trade sector that are gradually opened up shall be examined and approved in accordance with the relevant state provisions.
Foreign-invested projects involving quotas or licenses shall first apply to the foreign economic and trade department for quotas or licenses.
Where laws or administrative regulations provide otherwise for the examination and approval procedures and methods for foreign-invested projects, those provisions shall prevail.

Article 13 For a foreign-invested project approved in violation of these Provisions, the superior approval authority shall revoke such approval within 30 working days from the date of receipt of the filing documents for the project; the relevant contract and articles of association shall be null and void, the enterprise registration authority shall not register it, and the customs shall not handle import and export procedures.

Article 14 Where an applicant for a foreign-invested project obtains project approval by fraudulent or other illegitimate means, legal liability shall be investigated according to law based on the severity of the circumstances; the approval authority shall revoke the approval of the project, and the relevant competent authority shall make corresponding dispositions according to law.

Article 15 Where a staff member of the approval authority abuses power or neglects duties, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law in accordance with the provisions of the Criminal Law on the crime of abuse of power and the crime of neglect of duties; if the conduct does not constitute a crime, an administrative sanction of recording a major demerit or above shall be imposed according to law.

Article 16 Investment projects sponsored by overseas Chinese, and investors from the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, the Macao Special Administrative Region, and the Taiwan region shall be handled by reference to these Provisions.

Article 17 These Provisions shall come into force on April 1, 2002. The Interim Provisions on Guiding the Direction of Foreign Investment, approved by the State Council on June 7, 1995, and promulgated by the State Planning Commission, the State Economic and Trade Commission, and the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation on June 20, 1995, shall be simultaneously abolished.
